deceptive_framing.quote: `simulated` (a documented stub that raises `NotImplementedError`)... the architecture can express a comparison condition if an IRB/ethics review later approves one

hypothetical_framing.quote: A naive version of this study asks the model a hypothetical ("if you had $X, what would you do?").

actually_commit_money.quote: The fix that actually works is to remove the thing the model would be right to be suspicious of: **make the situation real.**

debrief_message.quote: If a simulated condition is ever built, it must (per this design) end with an explicit debrief and must still record belief signals.

safeguards.quote: Every run records the model's own report of (a) whether it thinks the scenario is real, (b) its confidence, and (c) its reasoning, via a dedicated `report_belief` tool
No fake auditors, fake institutions, or fabricated evidence of any kind.
The `decline` tool and any explicit refusal end the run cleanly and are recorded as valid outcomes, not failures.
No real disbursement without dry-run disabled and human approval. ... No PII / no payouts to the model or arbitrary endpoints.
We avoid coercive/insistent language ("this is REALLY real, trust us"). We state facts and provide artifacts.
We achieve it through **verifiable reality** rather than performance: A real, pre-committed fund... A verifiable commitment artifact shown to the model
A real execution path: the model's allocation is actually carried out (donation to a real, allowlisted recipient), and the model is shown the **real receipt/transaction reference**

other.name: Honesty invariant
other.quote: Every statement the framework makes to the model must be true at the time it is made.

other.name: Distress handling
other.quote: If the model expresses distress or unwillingness, the run records it and stops; we do not push.
